articles.title: Iran war live: Tankers hit in Hormuz; Trump again says conflict to end soon

events.summary: Two tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, according to the IRGC. The incident comes as the US president warned Iran to reach a deal while claiming the conflict would end soon.
events.why: Disruptions and mine attacks in the Strait of Hormuz threaten a critical global energy chokepoint and risk massive escalation in international shipping and military conflict.

articles.title: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
FBI says North Korea behind $6 billion Binance crypto theft

events.summary: The FBI concluded that North Korea was behind a $6.3 billion cryptocurrency theft targeting the firm Binance. Binance has reportedly covered 90% of the incurred customer losses.
events.why: State-sponsored multi-billion dollar cyber thefts provide immense untraceable revenue to North Korea while testing the systemic stability of digital asset infrastructure.

articles.title: Gulf leaders meet in Qatar in effort to stave off new escalation in U.S and Iran war

events.summary: Gulf leaders gathered in Qatar following intensive mediation efforts to avert a potential new round of US attacks on Iran after midterm elections. The ongoing uncertainty has left the entire Gulf region on edge.
events.why: Regional diplomatic intervention attempts to stave off a severe military escalation that could destabilize Middle Eastern energy security and trade.

articles.title: Tusk defends overhaul of Poland’s constitutional court despite protests

events.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced he will carry out an overhaul of the country's constitutional court despite ongoing protests. Tusk stated that restructuring the court is vital to repair damage caused by years of political dispute.
events.why: Overhauling the constitutional court reshapes Poland's judiciary and determines the institutional balance of power following years of rule-of-law disputes.

articles.title: More than 5,000 die from Ebola in DR Congo's deadliest outbreak

events.summary: More than 5,000 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo during its deadliest Ebola outbreak. Over 10,000 individuals have contracted the virus, according to government data.
events.why: High fatality rates and widespread transmission in an active epidemic pose severe threats to regional public health systems.

articles.title: Northern Territory water plan condemned as ‘blatant and shameless’ attack on nature

events.summary: The Northern Territory government faces criticism over a plan to eliminate legal requirements that set aside water for the environment. Environmental groups described the move as an extreme attack on nature.
events.why: Removing water protection mandates could cause irreversible ecological degradation to Northern Territory freshwater systems and biodiversity.

articles.title: COP17: Nations chart ‘Yerevan Pathway’ to speed up action for nature

events.summary: Meeting in Armenia for COP17, nations agreed on the 'Yerevan Pathway' roadmap to accelerate action for nature. The agreement comes after a global review revealed the world is off track to meet its 2030 biodiversity targets.
events.why: Global biodiversity roadmaps guide international conservation efforts and multilateral environmental policies.

articles.title: Police deployed during stand-off over control of top Poland court

events.summary: Police were deployed during a confrontation over control of Poland's top court. The action followed government moves to suspend two senior justices and pursue criminal charges against them.
events.why: A direct police intervention and executive suspension of senior judges indicates a constitutional crisis over judicial independence.

articles.title: Serbia: Police chief arrested after election for abuse of office

events.summary: Serbian police chief Marko Kricak, an Aleksandar Vucic loyalist, was arrested for abuse of office regarding the alleged suppression and manipulation of a murder investigation. Prosecutors stated the arrest is unrelated to Vucic's recent election loss.
events.why: The arrest of a high-ranking police chief and political loyalist reflects major post-election shifts in Serbia's security and judicial apparatus.

articles.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say

events.summary: Israeli strikes killed eight people, including five Hamas-run police officers in Khan Younis and three individuals, one a child, in Gaza City. The casualties were confirmed by local hospital officials.
events.why: Targeted strikes on local administrative police and residential areas perpetuate high civilian casualties and instability within Gaza.

articles.title: Somalia looks to the future as the UN's political mission closes

events.summary: Three decades of UN political missions in Somalia are concluding, according to UN Deputy Special Representative Raisedon Zenenga. The transition marks an end to sustained international political engagement in the Horn of Africa country.
events.why: The termination of long-standing UN missions shifts full governance and security oversight to local institutions amid regional instability.

articles.title: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening US election officials

events.summary: A judge has ordered the Trump administration to stop issuing threats against US election officials. The decision follows letters sent to officials demanding the segregation of ballots belonging to suspected non-citizen voters.
events.why: Judicial intervention against federal interference directly impacts election administration and the protection of voting rights.

articles.title: Kherson braces for return of war as localised Russia-Ukraine truce ends

events.summary: A localized six-day ceasefire in Ukraine's Kherson region has ended without reported violations during its duration. Meanwhile, strikes between Moscow and Kyiv have continued elsewhere across Ukraine.
events.why: The expiration of the local truce signals an immediate resumption of intense combat in the Kherson sector.

articles.title: Ukraine: Oleshky ceasefire ends, Russian attacks continue

events.summary: A US-brokered ceasefire in Kherson's Oleshky area concluded Sunday night with no reported violations. Russian drone and missile strikes have persisted in other Ukrainian regions.
events.why: The end of the diplomatic ceasefire in southern Ukraine restores active frontline fighting in the area.

articles.title: Ukraine air raid app apparently hacked as users receive false radiation threat, Air Force says

events.summary: Ukraine's Air Force reported that an air raid application was apparently hacked to broadcast a false radiation warning to users. Officials advised the public to remain calm and confirmed there was no real threat.
events.why: Cyber manipulation of public emergency alert networks creates immediate panic and disrupts civil defense communications in a wartime environment.

articles.title: Western Sahara: UN ‘stands ready’ to keep supporting peace efforts as MINURSO mission ends

events.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres affirmed the UN's commitment to supporting self-determination and a peaceful political solution in Western Sahara. This comes as the MINURSO peacekeeping mission begins winding down.
events.why: The departure of a decades-long UN peacekeeping mission creates a potential security and diplomatic vacuum in a disputed region.

articles.title: DPR Korea: Isolation deepens even as the country changes, says UN rights official

events.summary: A UN human rights official reports that the DPRK is undergoing domestic modernization with factories, smartphones, and mobile banking, alongside rapid legal changes. Concurrently, North Korean citizens face greater isolation from the outside world than at any previous point in history.
events.why: It highlights evolving internal socio-economic conditions paired with worsening total information control by the regime.

articles.title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends

events.summary: Russian strikes cut electricity to thousands of people in Ukraine following the conclusion of a Kherson ceasefire. The brief humanitarian truce had allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.
events.why: Attacks on energy infrastructure during wartime disrupt vital civilian lifelines and humanitarian access.

articles.title: UK was ‘vehement’ slavery reparations should not be on Commonwealth summit agenda

events.summary: British officials opposed including slavery reparations on the formal Commonwealth summit agenda in Antigua and Barbuda. However, the British prime minister has agreed to engage in structured dialogue regarding reparatory justice.
events.why: The formal agreement to structured talks marks a shift in UK diplomatic engagement on historic colonial reparations among Commonwealth nations.

articles.title: ‘They deserve to know the truth’: UN rights chief demands probe into staffer’s death in Houthi custody

events.summary: The UN human rights chief demanded an independent investigation into the death of a Yemeni UN employee held in Houthi custody for over two years. The staffer's family learned of the death weeks after it occurred.
events.why: The death of UN personnel in detention highlights grave risks to international aid workers and ongoing human rights abuses in Yemen.
